version.description: The version ocx reports for itself.

registry.description: The default registry a bare identifier resolves against.

platforms.description: The host platform as ocx matches it, `os.features` included.

features.description:
The host's full `os.features` (a superset of `libc`); a package is
runnable when its offered features are a subset of these.

libc.description:
Detected host libc `os.features` tags (e.g. `["libc.glibc"]`,
`["libc.glibc","libc.musl"]`), empty when none detected (non-Linux,
NixOS, failed probe). Reflects the same host detection the
index-resolution path uses; a host may advertise multiple families.

shell.description: The shell ocx detected; absent when it detected none.

channel.description: The release channel the binary was built for (`dev`, `stable`).

commit.description: The git commit the binary was built from.

ci.description: The CI run that built the binary.

About.description:
System information about the ocx installation.

The build-provenance blocks are absent on a local `cargo build` without
git, as in `ocx version --format json`.

Platform.description: An OCI image-spec platform object. `Platform::Any` writes os and architecture as "any".

os.version.description: Operating system version the image requires.

os.features.description: Features the image requires of the host (`libc.glibc`, …).

AbsolutePath.description: Absolute path in the native spelling of the host that wrote it.

dirty.description: `true` if the working tree had uncommitted changes when built.

CommitInfo.description: Git commit metadata baked at build time.

target.description: Target triple the binary was compiled for.

BuildInfo.description: Build environment metadata (timestamp, profile, target, rustc).

run_url.description:
Direct link to the run that produced this binary.
Composed as `{server_url}/{repository}/actions/runs/{run_id}`.

ref.description: The git ref the run built (`refs/tags/v1.2.3`).

sha.description: The commit SHA the run built.

CiInfo.description:
GitHub Actions context. Present only when built under a GitHub
workflow that exported the standard `GITHUB_*` env vars.

status.description:
`unchanged` when the rebuilt root was byte-identical to the committed
one, so nothing was committed; `updated` otherwise. An unchanged
`--fork` run still ensures a pull request when its announce branch is
ahead of the index base, and still reports one when the branch has
diverged from the index base but its open pull request can still
merge.

desc_status.description:
`updated` when the package's `__ocx.desc` artifact moved, so the
root's `desc` object was rebuilt and its readme (and logo) written as
new content-addressed objects; `unchanged` when the description sits
where the committed root already recorded it, or there is none.

credential_kind.description:
The API credential's kind. `job_token` only when the credential is
this environment's own `CI_JOB_TOKEN` — ocx cannot tell a personal from
a project, group or OAuth token, so it reports no kind it cannot
observe.

push_credential_kind.description:
The push credential's kind; absent under the `api` transport, which
pushes nothing. `git_helper` means nothing was injected and git's own
credential helpers authenticated the push.

branch.description:
The announce branch; absent under `--output`, which opens no request and
so has no branch.

pull_request_url.description:
The opened or updated pull request's web URL.

Always absent for `--output`. In `--fork` mode absent only when the run made
no pull request: an unchanged run whose announce branch is ahead of the
index base still ensures, and therefore reports, one. So does an unchanged
run whose branch has diverged from the index base but still holds an open,
mergeable pull request.

pull_request_number.description:
The opened or updated pull request's number; absent under the same
conditions as `pull_request_url`.

fork.description:
The verified fork, as `owner/repo`; absent for `--output`, and in `--fork`
mode only when the run made no pull request.

written_paths.description: The relative paths written under the `--output` directory; empty outside `--output`.

capability_checks.description:
Every preflight row, including the ones that did not apply.

Non-empty on every run, so a pipeline can assert the preflight ran rather
than trusting a bare success. Inapplicable rows carry `skipped`; rows
follow a fixed capability order, so the array is stable across runs.

reserved_tags_dropped.description:
Tags dropped from the curated set because they are reserved.

The OCX-internal `__ocx` namespace (which carries the keep tag) and the
frozen legacy `<algorithm>.<hex>` keep tags. Neither names a version, so
announce drops them and reports them here rather than failing the run.
Always an array, empty rather than absent.

removed.description:
Tags whose rows this run removed from the index because the registry no
longer has them. Always an array, empty rather than absent.

durable_missing.description:
Durable tags the registry no longer has, found by `--refresh` or
`--tags-from-registry` and kept in the index; name them with `--tags` or
`--tags-file` to remove them. Always an array, empty rather than absent.

AnnounceReport.description:
Result of a successful `ocx package announce`.

Plain format: a one-row table (`Package`, `Status`, `Pull Request`, `Fork`,
`Written Paths`); a dash marks a field the mode did not produce, and
`Written Paths` is a count, not the list. Every other key is JSON-only; the
command warns about dropped reserved tags on stderr when there are any.

JSON format: an object with one key per field below, in that order; a key
whose value the run did not produce is omitted.

WriteStatus.description: Whether a forge write moved anything.

x-ocx-enum.description: The committed or proposed content already matched, so nothing was written.
The run created or moved the content.

Forge.description: The forge the run wrote to, after `--forge`.

x-ocx-enum.description: GitHub.com or a GitHub Enterprise Server instance.
GitLab.com or a self-managed GitLab instance.

Transport.description: The write transport the run used.

x-ocx-enum.description: The forge's REST API.
A local `git` clone and one authenticated push.

CredentialKind.description:
The API credential's kind.

ocx reports only a kind it can observe: a personal access token, a deploy
token and an OAuth token all report as `token`.

x-ocx-enum.description: The credential is this environment's own `CI_JOB_TOKEN`.
A credential ocx holds but cannot classify further.
The ladder resolved nothing — the unauthenticated `--output` path.

PushCredentialKind.description:
The push credential's kind; absent when the `api` transport pushed nothing.

`git_helper` is a different statement: a push happened and git's own
credential helpers authenticated it.

x-ocx-enum.description: The push secret is this environment's own `CI_JOB_TOKEN`.
A push secret ocx injected but cannot classify further.
Nothing was injected; git's own credential helpers are in charge.

name.description: The capability this row reports on.

status.description: How the check came out.

detail.description: A human-readable qualifier where the forge exposes one.

CapabilityCheckEntry.description: One row of the write preflight.

x-ocx-enum.description: The local `git` version against the floor the git transport needs.
The credential's push permission on the repository being written.
Whether the project lets a CI job token push to its repository.
Whether the index project's job-token allowlist admits the publishing project.

CapabilityStatus.description:
How one capability check came out. There is no `failed`: a check that fails raises an error
and no report is rendered.

x-ocx-enum.description: The capability was read and is present.
The forge did not let the credential read the capability; never fails the run.
The check does not apply to this run's forge, transport or credential.

identifier.description: The package that was attested, resolved against the default registry.

platform.description:
The `--platform` the run narrowed into; absent when none was given and
the run attested whatever the identifier resolved to.

subject_digest.description: Digest of the subject manifest the Statement names.

predicate_type.description: The resolved `predicateType` URI written into the Statement.

bundle_digest.description:
Digest of the referrer's layer content: the Sigstore bundle blob on a
signed attach, the SBOM document itself on an unsigned one. The JSON key
keeps its shipped name.

referrer_digest.description: Digest of the published OCI referrer manifest wrapping the payload.

sidecar_digest.description:
Digest of the `sha256-<hex>.att` sidecar manifest, when
`--signature-format` asked for one.

signed.description:
Whether the referrer carries a signature. `false` means the document was
attached as-is, with no identity behind it — the two certificate fields
below are then absent rather than empty.

certificate_identity.description: Certificate SAN (identity) embedded in the Fulcio cert.

certificate_oidc_issuer.description: Certificate OIDC issuer URL embedded in the Fulcio cert.

key_backend.description:
Which key model produced this attestation (`keyless`, `file`, and —
once they exist — `aws_kms` and friends). Absent on an unsigned attach,
where no key model was involved at all. Same vocabulary as the
`ocx package sign` report.

public_key_hint.description: The signing key's cosign hint, in key mode only.

transparency_log_index.description:
The Rekor log index of the transparency record this run created.

Absent when no record was created: legal under a key, where
`--rekor-upload` is opt-in, and on an unsigned attach.

AttestationReport.description:
Summary of a successful keyless attestation.

Digests are always full in JSON. `bundle_digest` and `referrer_digest`
describe the OCI 1.1 referrer and are absent under `--signature-format
simplesigning`, which publishes only the `sha256-<hex>.att` sidecar that
`sidecar_digest` names. `predicate_type` is the **resolved** URI, not the
`--type` spelling passed: alias resolution decides what is published,
annotated and hashed, and echoing it keeps that resolution visible.

KeyBackendKind.description:
What produced or verified a signature — the frozen `signatures[].key_backend`
vocabulary.

x-ocx-enum.description: A Fulcio-issued ephemeral certificate; no long-lived key.
A key read from the filesystem.
A key PEM held in an environment variable.
AWS KMS.
Google Cloud KMS.
Azure Key Vault.
HashiCorp Vault transit.
A Kubernetes secret.

items.description: One entry per repository: in registry order without `--with-tags`, sorted by name with it.

Catalog.description:
Repository catalog listing, optionally including tags per repository.

Plain format: one-column table (Repository) without tags, or two-column
table (Repository | Tag) when tags are included.

tags.description: The repository's tags, sorted; present only when tags were requested.

name.description: The logical name written into the root.

status.description:
`unchanged` when the open claim branch already carries a
byte-identical root; `updated` otherwise, which `--output` always is.

credential_kind.description:
The API credential's kind. `job_token` only when the credential is
this environment's own `CI_JOB_TOKEN` — ocx cannot tell a personal from
a project, group or OAuth token, so it reports no kind it cannot
observe.

push_credential_kind.description:
The push credential's kind; absent under the `api` transport, which
pushes nothing. `git_helper` means nothing was injected and git's own
credential helpers authenticated the push.

author.description:
The identity that authored the request; absent when none is available.

The token identity, else the CI-environment identity; distinct from
`owners`, as authorship is not ownership. **Not attested**: the second rung
is an ordinary environment read (`GITLAB_USER_LOGIN`/`GITLAB_USER_ID`, else
`GITHUB_ACTOR`/`GITHUB_ACTOR_ID`) an earlier pipeline step can set to
anything; only the first rung is the forge's own answer about the
credential. A consumer must not treat this key as an attestation of who ran
the command; `author_identity_source` says which rung answered.

author_identity_source.description:
Which rule produced `author`: `resolved` or `ci_environment`; absent exactly when `author` is.

`resolved` means the forge's own answer about the credential, and
`ci_environment` the CI pair. The key makes `author` usable: the login
alone cannot say whether the forge asserted it or a pipeline step wrote it
into an environment variable, and a governance consumer needs that
difference. `asserted` is unreachable here: no operator word is ever
taken for the author.

owners.description: The resolved owner list written into the root, in the order given.

branch.description:
The claim branch, so a script need not re-derive the naming convention.
Always present, `--output` included: the name is derived from the package,
not read from the forge, so a run that opens no request still reports
the branch a later run would use.

pull_request_url.description: The opened or updated request's web URL; absent when the run opened none.

pull_request_number.description: The opened or updated request's number; absent when the run opened none.

fork.description:
The verified fork, as `namespace/project`; absent on the direct path and
under the `git` transport.

written_paths.description: The relative paths written under the `--output` directory; empty otherwise.

capability_checks.description:
Every preflight row, including the ones that did not apply.

Non-empty on every run, so a pipeline can assert the preflight ran rather
than trusting a bare success. Inapplicable rows carry `skipped`; rows
follow a fixed capability order, so the array is stable across runs.

ClaimReport.description:
Result of a successful `ocx package claim`.

Plain format: a one-row table (`Package`, `Status`, `Transport`, `Branch`,
`Pull Request`); a dash marks a field the run did not produce. `owners`,
`author`, `author_identity_source` and `capability_checks` are JSON-only.

JSON format: an object with one key per field below, in that order; a key
whose value the run did not produce is omitted. `status` compares against the
open claim branch, not the committed root, so a claim `--output` run is always
`updated`, where an announce `--output` run can report `unchanged`.

id.description: The forge's immutable numeric account id.

OwnerEntry.description:
One forge account, as the claim root spells it.

The same `{login, id}` shape the root file writes, so a consumer comparing
the report against the committed entry compares like with like. Never a bare
login: an id is what survives a rename.

x-ocx-enum.description: The forge answered: its users API, or its own account behind the credential.
A `LOGIN:ID` pair was taken on the operator's word because the users API was unreachable.
The CI environment's variables named the identity.

items.description: One entry per resource: objects, then temp directories, then consent stamps.

Clean.description: Objects, temp directories and consent stamps a clean removed, or would remove in a dry run.

kind.description: What kind of resource this is.

dry_run.description: Whether the run was a dry run, so nothing was removed.

path.description: Where the resource is, or was.

held_by.description:
Project `ocx.lock` paths holding this entry. Empty when the entry is not
protected by any registered project, or when `--force` was specified.

CleanEntry.description:
A single cleaned-up resource entry.

The `held_by` field lists the absolute paths of every registered project's
`ocx.lock` that pins this package. Non-empty only for `object` kind entries
in dry-run mode when the package would have been collected without the
project registry. Empty in non-dry-run output (held entries are never
collected) and always empty for `temp` and `consent` entries.

CleanKind.description: The kind of resource cleaned up.

x-ocx-enum.description: An unreferenced package in the object store.
A leftover temporary directory.
A `state/projects/<key>/` directory whose consent stamp was swept.

managed_config.description: The adoption outcome, in the entry shape `ocx self setup` reports.

ConfigSetupData.description:
Report of `ocx config setup`: the outcome of adopting the managed config.

Plain format: a key/value table with a `Managed config` summary row.

status.description: What the run did to the managed-config tier.

digest.description: The adopted snapshot's digest, on every status that has one.

previous_digest.description: The digest the snapshot carried before a `refreshed` run.

reason.description: Why a `refresh_unavailable` run could not reach the registry.

ManagedConfigEntry.description: The managed-config adoption outcome, shared by `ocx self setup` and `ocx config setup`.

ManagedConfigStatusKind.description: What a run did to the managed-config tier.

x-ocx-enum.description: No managed config is configured.
The snapshot was already adopted and current.
A snapshot was fetched and adopted.
The adopted snapshot was replaced by a newer one.
The registry could not be reached; the adopted snapshot is kept.
The managed-config tier was removed.
The managed block in `config.toml` carried user edits and was left untouched.
Dry run: a snapshot would be adopted.
Dry run: the adopted snapshot would be refreshed.

candidate.description: The candidate file this report describes.

valid.description:
Always `true`: an invalid payload fails the command (exit 78) and
produces no report. Carried so a JSON consumer reads the verdict from
the document rather than inferring it from the exit code.

plain_http.description:
Hosts this machine would contact over plain HTTP once the candidate is
adopted, sorted — the candidate's own `[registries.<name>] insecure`
entries unioned with this machine's `OCX_INSECURE_REGISTRIES`, less
anything the system scope locked shut.

The gate already computes this set to validate the payload's mirrors;
reporting it is what makes "did my entry take effect?" a one-command
question. A key that is not an exact `host[:port]` grants nothing and
simply will not appear here.

patches.description:
Effective `[patches]` tier, defaults applied.

Same precedence every ocx invocation uses: the merged config tier when
it declares `[patches]`, else the forwarded `OCX_PATCHES` env tier. A
candidate declaring `[patches]` therefore outranks an ambient
`OCX_PATCHES`, exactly as it would once adopted.

unknown_keys.description:
Dotted paths of keys the config schema ignores, sorted. Advisory: the
loader ignores unknown keys by design, so these are equally typos and
settings a newer ocx understands.

Keys inside a `[mirrors]` entry are NOT covered: that table is parsed
value-first from a raw TOML value, so nothing there is ever ignored by
the schema. A misspelled mirror role is silently dropped and reported
here as clean.

ConfigTestData.description:
CLI report for `ocx config test` — a candidate managed-config payload
validated locally, plus the configuration adopting it would produce.

Plain format: key/value table; rows with no payload are suppressed, and
list-valued fields render one row per value.

JSON format: the list fields are always present (`[]` when empty); `registry_default`,
`patches` and `managed` are omitted when the tier is unconfigured.

repository_prefix.description:
The `[patches] registry` value: the registry, and optionally a repository prefix, hosting
patch descriptors.

path_template.description: Path template for per-package patch repositories, placeholders intact.

required.description: Whether an unavailable companion fails the launch.

PatchesView.description:
The `[patches]` tier as it would resolve after the candidate merges —
defaults applied, so an omitted field is reported as the value that would
actually apply rather than as absent.

source.description: The effective managed-config source (env override, else the seed).

required.description: Whether an absent or mismatched snapshot fails commands closed.

ManagedView.description:
The machine's own `[managed]` tier posture.

Never the candidate's: a payload carrying a `[managed]` section is rejected
outright, so this answers "which tier would adopt this payload", not
"what does the payload declare".

status.description: What the run found or did.

source.description: The effective managed-config source (flag > env > seed).

fetched_at.description: When the snapshot was last fetched.

kill_switches.description: Active kill switches (e.g. `OCX_NO_CONFIG_REFRESH`), by env-var name.

drift.description:
Whether the registry's current digest differs from the local
snapshot; present only when reachable (`--check`, online).

tag.description:
The tag the local snapshot was fetched under (snapshot v2 bookkeeping —
shows which floating/pinned tag the tier tracks).

pause_ends_at.description:
The instant until which the background tick is paused
(`ocx config update --pause`); absent when no pause is in force.

pinned.description:
The version spec pinned alongside an in-force pause
(`--pause <d> <VERSION>`); absent when the pause carries no pin.

ConfigUpdateData.description:
CLI report for `ocx config update` — both the full-update path and the
`--check` probe-only path (mirrors `ocx self update --check`).

Plain format: key/value table; rows with no payload are suppressed.

ConfigUpdateStatus.description:
Top-level `status` of the `ocx config update` report.

Each variant serializes as its `snake_case` name.

x-ocx-enum.description: No managed-config tier is configured.

The registry was probed and its digest matches the local snapshot —
verified current. Reported only when the probe actually ran.
A new snapshot was fetched and persisted (full-update path only).

A probe-only report (`--check`) that ran and detected drift — no swap
was attempted.

A probe-only report (`--check`) whose registry probe could NOT run —
offline, no client, source absent, auth failure, or a registry error.
Distinct from `already_current` so operators can tell "verified
current" apart from "couldn't check" — the report degrades to
local-state only (source/digest/fetched-at, no live drift).

Timestamp.description: RFC 3339 instant in UTC (`Z`), whole seconds.

items.description: One tree per requested package, in request order.

DependencyTree.description: Tree view of the dependency graph (default output).

repeated.description: Whether this package already appeared earlier in the tree; its dependencies are listed there.

visibility.description: The visibility the parent declared for this edge, not the propagated result; absent on a root.

DependencyNode.description: A node in the dependency tree (for tree view output).

Visibility.description: Two-axis visibility of a dependency edge or env entry: whether it reaches the package's own runtime, its consumers, both or neither.

x-ocx-enum.description: Visible to neither the package's own runtime nor its consumers.
Visible to the package's own runtime only.
Visible to the package's own runtime and to consumers.
Visible to consumers only.

paths.description: Every path from a requested root to the target, root first.

message.description: Why no path was found; present only when `paths` is empty.

DependenciesTrace.description: Why view — all paths from roots to a target dependency.

items.description: Every dependency in resolution order.

FlatDependencies.description: Flat view of the resolved dependency order.

visibility.description: The dependency's resolved visibility; a requested root is `public`.

FlatDependency.description: One dependency in the flat view.

items.description: The resolved entries, in application order.

binaries.description: Admitted `binaries` claims, attributed to their packages.

entrypoints.description: Admitted `entrypoints` claims, attributed to their packages.

integrations.description: Admitted integration payloads, one per (package, namespace) pair.

advisories.description:
Advisories raised for the **deferred** tools in this composition —
always present, empty whenever nothing was deferred. Warning-only.

EnvVars.description:
Resolved environment variables for one or more packages, in declaration order.

Each `items` entry carries its modifier `kind`: `constant` replaces any
existing value for the key, `path` prepends using the platform path separator.
A key may appear more than once, with different kinds.

JSON format: `{"items", "binaries", "entrypoints", "integrations",
"advisories"}`, each always present as an array, possibly empty. The last four
are top-level siblings, never nested inside `items`, and `integrations` is
never collapsed for a single root.

value.description: The resolved value this entry contributes.

kind.description: How the value combines with the variable's existing value.

separator.description: The separator a `list` entry folds with; absent on every other kind.

source.description:
Origin annotation under `--show-patches`: absent for a package-native
entry, the patch provenance object for a companion overlay entry.

EnvEntry.description:
A single resolved environment variable entry, tagged with its modifier kind.

`source` is present only under `--show-patches`, and only for an entry that
came from a companion overlay. `separator` carries the fold separator of a
`list` entry, absent only when nothing in the composition declared one;
every other kind omits it.

ModifierKind.description: How a declared value combines with the variable's existing value.

x-ocx-enum.description: Prepended to any existing value of the variable.
Replaces any existing value of the variable.
Appended to any existing value of the variable, joined by its separator.

oneOf.description: Declared by the package itself.

rule.description: The descriptor rule glob that admitted the companion for the base.

companion.description: The identifier of the companion that produced the entry.

oneOf.description: Contributed by a companion patch overlay.

EntrySource.description:
Origin of a resolved environment variable entry, shown under `--show-patches`.

A package-native entry has no `source` object at all. A companion patch
overlay entry carries `{"type": "patch", "rule": "<glob>", "companion":
"<companion-id>"}`, exactly these three keys.

name.description: The claimed executable or entrypoint name.

package.description: The declaring package; absent when attribution is unknown.

BinaryAttribution.description:
A single admitted `binaries`/`entrypoints` claim, attributed to the
package that declared it.

An absent `package` means "attribution unknown", never "this package has
zero binaries".

namespace.description: The integration namespace the payload is keyed under.

package.description: The declaring package; absent when attribution is unknown.

payload.description: The interpolated payload, emitted exactly as composed.

IntegrationAttribution.description:
One admitted integration contribution, attributed to the declaring
package.

`payload` is the interpolated payload, arbitrary JSON OCX does not
interpret. An absent `package` means "attribution unknown", never "no
payload". One row per (package, namespace) pair: an array longer than the
distinct-namespace count is the structural guarantee that nothing merged.

package.description: The deferred package the advisory concerns.

key.description: The environment variable the advisory names; present for the two variable kinds.

message.description: The human rendering of the advisory.

LazyAdvisoryReport.description:
One advisory raised while composing a **deferred** tool, in wire shape.

`kind` is the machine discriminator — a consumer branches on it and never
on `message`, which is the human rendering of the same fact. `key` is
present only for the two variants that name an environment variable.

Advisories are warning-only and never fail a compose. They flag a deferred
tool's declared metadata that will not substitute cleanly until its content
materializes.

x-ocx-enum.description:
A `constant` or `list` variable interpolating `${installPath}`, which a tool may read before the package
is materialized.
No `binaries` claim, so the deferred tool's launcher names cannot be enumerated.
A `path` value combining `${installPath}` with anything else, which the launcher cannot substitute.

items.description: One entry per registry, in argument order.

CatalogPreview.description: What `ocx index sync --dry-run` would refresh, per registry, in argument order.

registry.description: The registry the packages were enumerated from.

packages.description: The packages a sync would refresh, sorted.

items.description: One entry per registry, in argument order.

RegenerateReport.description: What `ocx index regenerate <REGISTRY>...` changed, per registry, in argument order.

registry.description: The registry whose catalog was rebuilt.

roots.description: The root documents the `p/` walk found.

corrected.description: Packages whose catalog row was rewritten.

RegenerateEntry.description:
One registry's drift-repair outcome.

`roots` is what the `p/` walk found, and it is reported even when the three
lists are empty: a `0` there says the walk found an empty tree, which is a
different fact from "the catalog already matched".

packages.description: One entry per package, keyed by the identifier as given, sorted by key.

Installs.description:
Installed or selected packages.

The plain `Version` column drops the digest; the pinned form stays in JSON.

identifier.description: The pinned identifier the package resolved to.

path.description: The symlink written; absent when no host symlink was written.

InstallEntry.description:
A single install or select result entry for CLI output.

The `path` field holds the symlink that was created or updated (candidate
for install, current for select). It is absent when no host symlink was
written: a foreign-platform install populates the object store but writes
neither host pointer.

Metadata.description:
OCX package metadata.

Declares a package's type, extraction options, environment variables, and
dependencies. Currently only the `bundle` type is supported.

x-ocx-enum.description: The first bundle metadata format.

Env.description: A package's declared environment variables, in declaration order.

visibility.description:
Visibility on the entry axis — controls which exec surface (interface vs private)
sees this entry. Defaults to `private` — publishers explicitly mark
contract entries as `public` or `interface` to expose them to consumers.
`"sealed"` is rejected at parse time.

x-ocx-enum.description: Visible to the package's own runtime only.
Visible to the package's own runtime and to consumers.
Visible to consumers only.

oneOf.description: A path variable is prepended to any existing value of the environment variable.
A constant variable replaces any existing value of the environment variable.

A list variable is appended to any existing value of the environment
variable, joined by its own separator, with earlier occurrences of the
same contribution removed.

Var.description:
An environment variable declaration.

Each variable has a key (the variable name), a modifier that determines
how the value is resolved, and a visibility that controls which exec
surfaces load the entry. The modifier's type and fields are flattened into
this object in JSON.

`visibility` defaults to `private`: publishers must opt in explicitly to
expose entries on the consumer axis. `"sealed"` is rejected at parse time —
a variable invisible on every surface is dead config.

required.description:
Whether the resolved path must exist on disk. If `true` and the path is missing, installation fails.
Defaults to `false`.

value.description:
The value template. `${installPath}` — or its alias `${self.installPath}` — is this package's
content directory, `${deps.NAME.installPath}` a declared dependency's, and `${self.env.KEY}` the
resolved value of a variable declared earlier in this same list. Append `:native` or `:posix` to
pick the path style. Every other `${...}` is rejected; write `$${` for a literal `${`.

Path.description:
A path-type environment variable.

Path variables are prepended to any existing value of the environment variable.
Interpolation tokens in `value` are replaced at resolution time.

value.description:
The value template. `${installPath}` — or its alias `${self.installPath}` — is this package's
content directory, `${deps.NAME.installPath}` a declared dependency's, and `${self.env.KEY}` the
resolved value of a variable declared earlier in this same list. Append `:native` or `:posix` to
pick the path style. Every other `${...}` is rejected; write `$${` for a literal `${`.

Constant.description:
A constant-type environment variable.

Constant variables replace any existing value of the environment variable.
Interpolation tokens in `value` are replaced at resolution time.

separator.description:
The string joining this contribution to the variable's existing value —
a single space for `JDK_JAVA_OPTIONS`, a comma for `GODEBUG`.

Required in package metadata; `ocx.toml` and `ocx exec --env` may omit it.

value.description:
The value template. `${installPath}` — or its alias `${self.installPath}` — is this package's
content directory, `${deps.NAME.installPath}` a declared dependency's, and `${self.env.KEY}` the
resolved value of a variable declared earlier in this same list. Append `:native` or `:posix` to
pick the path style. Every other `${...}` is rejected; write `$${` for a literal `${`.

List.description:
A list-type environment variable.

List variables are appended to any existing value of the environment
variable, with every earlier occurrence of the same contribution removed
first, so re-applying moves the contribution to the back rather than
duplicating it. Interpolation tokens in `value` are replaced at
resolution time.

The contribution is opaque: ocx never splits it into elements, so a value
carrying the separator is still one contribution.

Dependencies.description: Ordered list of package dependencies; array position is the environment import order.

identifier.description:
Fully qualified pinned OCX identifier with required explicit registry
and digest. The tag portion is advisory (for update tooling) — only
the digest is used for resolution.

visibility.description:
Controls how this dependency's environment variables propagate.
Default: `sealed` — no env contribution. One of four levels: `sealed`,
`private`, `public`, `interface`.

name.description:
Optional name for this dependency used in `${deps.NAME.installPath}` interpolation.

When set, overrides the default name (last path segment of the OCI repository).
Use to resolve collisions when two dependencies share the same repository basename.

Dependency.description:
A pinned dependency descriptor.

The digest references either an OCI Image Index (for platform-aware
resolution) or a single manifest (for explicit platform pinning).
For cross-compilation, pin the platform-specific manifest digest directly.

PinnedPackageRef.description: Pinned OCI identifier with a required digest and an optional advisory tag: 'registry/repository[:tag]@digest'.

DependencyName.description: Interpolation name for this dependency. Must match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*$ (max 64 chars).

Entrypoints.description: Map of entrypoint names to entrypoint definitions. Each key is the user-invokable command name; the value object carries an optional `command` field naming the binary the generated launcher dispatches to when it differs from the invokable name (omit it and the name is dispatched directly). An optional `args` array supplies fixed leading arguments the generated launcher prepends before user args; each element may carry `${installPath}` (or its alias `${self.installPath}`), optionally suffixed `:native` or `:posix`, while `${deps.*}` and `${self.env.*}` are not permitted in args and every other `${...}` is rejected — write `$${` for a literal `${`.

command.description:
Dispatch target resolved on the composed `PATH`, when it differs from
the invocable name. Absent means the entrypoint name *is* the command
(the common case): a package may expose `hello` while dispatching a
differently named binary such as `hello-bin`.

args.description:
Fixed leading arguments the generated launcher prepends before the user's
own arguments. Each element may carry `${installPath}` — or its alias
`${self.installPath}` — optionally suffixed `:native` or `:posix`; `${deps.*}`
and `${self.env.*}` are NOT permitted here, and every other `${...}` is rejected
(write `$${` for a literal `${`). Absent/empty serializes to nothing.

Entrypoint.description:
A single named entrypoint for a package.

The map key in `entrypoints` supplies the *invocable name* — the filename
of the generated launcher; this object holds the per-entry value. The
launcher re-enters via `ocx launcher exec '<package-root>' -- <name> [args...]`,
preserving clean-env execution semantics, and resolves the *dispatch
command* against the composed `PATH` from the package's `env` block:
`command` when set, otherwise the invocable name itself.

EntrypointName.description: Entrypoint name for invocation by users. Must match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*$ and be at most 64 characters.

Binaries.description: Publisher-declared, unverified claim of interface-surface executable names exposed on PATH by this package. Absent means undeclared; an empty array means the publisher asserts zero interface binaries. On Windows the claim reflects the default executable-resolution set (.exe/.com/.bat/.cmd); a customized child PATHEXT may resolve fewer.

Integrations.description:
A package's declared `integrations` map: namespace key → opaque payload.

Absent on the wire and empty are the **same** state: nothing distinguishes
"declares none" from "did not say".

version.description:
The version of the bundle metadata format.
Reserved for future schema evolution.

strip_components.description:
Number of leading path components to strip when extracting the bundle.
This is a convenient feature for archives not created by OCX, which often contain a single top-level directory.
By default, OCX will not strip any components, and will extract the archive as-is.

env.description: Environment variables the package declares, in declaration order.

dependencies.description:
Ordered list of package dependencies, pinned by digest.
Array order defines environment import order.

entrypoints.description:
Named entrypoints that `ocx install` generates launchers for.

Each entry produces a Unix `.sh` script and, on Windows, a native
`.exe` shim plus its `.shim` sidecar under the package's
`entrypoints/` sibling directory at install time.
Absent or empty means no launchers are generated.

binaries.description:
Publisher-declared, unverified claim of interface-surface executable
names exposed on `PATH` by this package. Absent means undeclared
(predates this field); `[]` means the publisher asserts zero interface
binaries. Deliberately distinct wire states.

integrations.description:
Vendor-namespaced configuration blocks for tools OCX does not model.
Keys are namespaces (reverse-DNS by convention, not enforced); values
are opaque JSON OCX never interprets, merges, or validates the contents
of. Absent and empty are the same state.

Bundle.description:
Bundle package metadata.

Declares the format version, optional extraction options, environment variables,
dependencies, and entrypoints that OCX should expose when running commands with
this package.

items.description: The locked bindings, in lock order.

LockReport.description:
Report emitted by `ocx lock`, `ocx add` and `ocx remove`: every locked binding.

Plain format: three-column table (Binding | Group | Digest) of the host-platform leaf.

group.description: The owning group: `default` for the top-level `[tools]` table, else the `[group.*]` key.

digest.description: The host platform's leaf digest; absent when no leaf, or more than one, fits the host.

platform_digests.description:
Every leaf the lock records, keyed by the canonical platform string
(`os/arch[/variant][+feature,…]` or `any`).

LockEntry.description: One locked binding in the `ocx lock` report.

registry.description: The registry the credentials were stored for.

username.description: The user name the credentials were stored under.

LoginResult.description:
Successful `ocx login` result.

Plain format: nothing on stdout — the human "Login succeeded" line is a
stderr diagnostic emitted via `Api::success`. stdout is the CLI's
machine interface and stays empty when there is no parseable payload.

registry.description: The registry whose credentials were removed.

LogoutResult.description:
Successful `ocx logout` result.

Plain format: nothing on stdout; success is reported on stderr.

items.description: One report per package, in input order: its alias states, slot rows, index findings and ignored tags.

PackageCascadeCheck.description: What `cascade check` found, one entry per package in input order.

identifier.description: The physical repository the graph was read from.

logical.description: The logical name the user asked for, when it differed.

aliases.description: Per alias, what the registry holds as a whole.

rows.description:
Per-slot rows, sorted by (tag, platform). Includes `Ok` rows so a
reader sees the whole graph, not only its damage.

index_findings.description: Registry-versus-index findings; always empty for a physical identifier.

ignored_tags.description: Tags excluded from the graph, verbatim.

unrepairable.description: Findings that need new content published before they can be fixed.

CascadeReport.description:
The whole finding set for one package — the value both `check` and `repair`
report.

oneOf.description: An image index — the shape every alias is supposed to have.
No such tag at the registry: the alias was never created.

digest.description: The bare manifest the tag resolves to.

oneOf.description:
The tag exists but resolves to a bare image manifest, so it has no
per-platform slots at all and every expected platform reads as missing.

AliasState.description: What the registry holds at an alias tag, taken as a whole.

tag.description: The alias tag this slot belongs to.

status.description: The slot's verdict.

observed.description: The digest the alias carries for this platform; absent when it carries none.

expected.description: The digest the fold expects; absent when it expects none.

source.description: The version the expectation was folded from.

observed_source.description:
The version the observed digest belongs to, when the observed content
is recognisable as some published version's — absent when the alias
points at content no observed leaf carries.

SlotRow.description:
One row of the diff: what one alias holds for one platform versus what the
fold says it should hold.

Digests are the wire strings verbatim, an algorithm this build does not
implement included.

AliasTag.description: The registry tag itself, e.g. latest, 3, 3.28, 3.28.1, or a variant name.

SlotStatus.description: The verdict for one (alias, platform) slot.

x-ocx-enum.description: The alias carries exactly the expected entry.
The alias should carry a platform it does not carry at all.
The alias carries this platform, but not the expected content.

The alias carries a platform nothing folds into it — a leftover from
an earlier cascade. Reported always; removed only when the entry it
points at no longer exists.

The alias carries more than one entry for this platform. Only the last
one resolves, so a shadowed entry is invisible to every consumer while
still being published — including when the surviving one is exactly what
the fold expects. One row per shadowed entry, beside the row for the
entry that wins.

PackageVersion.description: An OCX package version, e.g. `3.28.1`, a rolling `3.28`, `0.5.0-canary` or a variant `debug-3.12.5`.

live.description: The digest the alias points at today.

oneOf.description:
The index committed a different digest than the alias points at today.
Repair cannot fix this — announcing the tag can.
The registry carries the alias and the index has never recorded it.

IndexFinding.description:
A disagreement between the registry graph and the public index that
publishes it.

Only ever produced for a logical identifier: a physical repository has no
reverse mapping back to an index root, so the layer is skipped entirely.

oneOf.description:
A planned entry points at a child manifest the registry no longer
holds, so writing the alias would publish a dangling pointer.

digest_text.description: The child digest exactly as the index writes it; no `Digest`, since this build cannot parse it.

oneOf.description:
A planned entry names a digest algorithm this build cannot address, so
whether the child is still there could not be checked at all. Distinct
from `child_manifest_missing`: nothing was observed to be gone —
the alias is refused because the check could not be made.

Repairing the alias would leave it with no entries at all. Refused:
an empty index is worse than a stale one.

Unrepairable.description:
Something check found that no repair can fix without new content being
published.

items.description:
One entry per package: the finding report, the planned writes, their outcomes and the `tags` this run
left present.

dry_run.description: True when nothing was written because the run was a preview.

tags_file.description: Where `--tags-file` was written; absent when the flag was not passed.

PackageCascadeRepair.description:
What `cascade repair` did, one entry per package in input order.

`dry_run` and `tags_file` are run-wide.

report.description: The package's findings, the same report `cascade check` prints.

planned.description: The alias writes this run planned.

outcomes.description: Empty for a preview run: nothing was attempted.

tags.description:
The alias tags this run left present in the registry - the same lines
written to `--tags-file`, echoed here so a JSON consumer gets them
without reading the file back.

RepairEntry.description:
One package's repair run: what was wrong, what the run planned, and what
the registry accepted.

`planned` and `outcomes` are separate: a preview has the first and not the
second, and a real run's outcomes can disagree with its plan (an alias
refused at preflight, a write the registry rejected).

index.description: The complete index to PUT at `tag`.

observed_digest.description:
The digest the alias points at now — absent when the alias does not
exist yet.

referenced_digests.description:
Every child manifest digest `index` references, deduped. Apply
preflights each one so a missing child refuses the alias instead of
publishing a dangling pointer.

reasons.description:
The rows that justify the write — what the user is being told changed.

Includes the alias's `orphan` rows even though an orphan never causes a
write on its own.

PlannedWrite.description:
One alias index to write, recomputed whole.

A repair never patches an alias in place: it rebuilds the entire index from
content the registry already serves and PUTs it, so the write is idempotent
and a partially-applied run leaves every untouched alias byte-identical.

RepairOutcome.description: What happened to one alias tag in a repair run.

digest.description: The digest of the index written.

verified.description: Whether the post-write read-back returned the same digest.

dropped.description:
The dead child digests dropped from the planned index before it went on the
wire, each backing nothing but orphan slots; absent when empty, as on every
ordinary write.

oneOf.description:
The index was written. `verified` is false when the post-write read-back
returned a different digest — a concurrent writer, which is a warning
rather than a failure: this run's write did land.

Refused before any write, because applying it would publish something
broken.

expected.description: The digest the plan expected; absent when the plan expected no alias.

live.description: The digest the alias holds now; absent when the alias is gone.

oneOf.description:
The alias moved between the gather this plan was computed from and the
write, so nothing was written. Not a fault and not unrepairable: a
publish landed in the middle of the run, and re-running the repair
against the new state is the whole fix.
The registry rejected the write, with the rendered cause.

WriteOutcome.description: The result of attempting one alias index write.

status.description: `copied`, or `planned` under `--dry-run`.

manifests.description:
One row per platform manifest the target offers after this copy,
including any it already had that the source does not ship.

cascade_tags_written.description: Rolling tags written in addition to the target's own tag.

keep_tags_written.description:
Digest-named `__ocx.keep.<algorithm>-<hex>` tags written, one per distinct
manifest.

referrers_copied.description: Referrer manifests carried over — signatures, SBOMs, attestations.

sidecar_conflicts.description:
Sidecar tags the target already held under a different manifest, and
this copy therefore refused to overwrite. Non-empty means exit 65.

blobs.description: Blob traffic, summed over every platform.

description.description:
What became of the repository description; absent when
`--with-description` was not passed.

CopyReport.description:
Result of `ocx package copy`.

`status` distinguishes a plan (`planned`, under `--dry-run`) from a
promotion; each row's `disposition` keeps its stable slug either way.

CopyStatus.description: Whether this run copied or only planned.

x-ocx-enum.description: The copy was written to the target.
`--dry-run`: the copy was planned and nothing was written.

digest.description:
The leaf digest the target serves for this platform. For a
`kept_not_in_source` row this is the digest it already had.

disposition.description:
Typed, so JSON carries `added` / `unchanged` / `replaced` /
`kept_not_in_source` while the table renders the prose.

Disposition.description: What became of one platform at the target.

x-ocx-enum.description: The target's index had no entry for this platform.
The target already pointed at this exact digest — nothing to do.
The target pointed at a different digest for this platform.

The target offers this platform and the source does not, so the merge
leaves it alone.

present.description: Already at the target — nothing transferred.

mounted.description: Mounted from another repository in the same registry.

uploaded.description: Downloaded from the source and uploaded to the target.

BlobSummary.description: Blob traffic, summed over every platform.

DescriptionOutcome.description:
What became of the repository description.

Reported as a field so a CI job reading `--format json` finds out whether
the catalog page travelled; a stderr warning is not a field.

x-ocx-enum.description: Pulled from the source and pushed to the target.

The source publishes none, so there was nothing to copy. Not a failure:
a description is repository-level prose and legitimately absent.
`--dry-run` was in force, so the description was not read or written.

descriptions.description: One entry per requested package, keyed by the identifier as given, in request order.

PackageDescriptions.description: The descriptions of every requested package.

published.description:
Whether the repository publishes a description; when `false` the three
fields below are absent.

keywords.description: The description's keywords annotation, as published.

InspectReport.description: The report `ocx inspect` and `ocx package inspect` emit.

platform.description: The platform the run selected; absent when it selected none.

packages.description: One entry per inspected package, in request order.

env.description: The composed project-tier environment in application order; empty when nothing applies.

PackageInspect.description: One inspected package. `pinned_identifier` and `pinned_digest` appear together, only when the entry pinned one artifact. The other keys come from one shape: `candidates` (an image index or an `ocx.lock` binding), `metadata` + `layers` (a manifest), or `platform` + `metadata` + `layers` + `resolution` (a resolved package); `closure` joins the last two under `--closure`.

name.description: The package as the caller addressed it.

pinned_identifier.description: The one artifact this entry pinned.

candidates.description: The platform children of an image index, or the platforms an `ocx.lock` binding pins.

layers.description: The selected manifest's layers, in order.

pinned.description:
This candidate as a pullable reference — the entry's identifier with
this child's digest attached. Emitted for the same reason the entry
carries `pinned_identifier`: splicing one by hand means knowing where
the tag goes relative to the digest.

media_type.description:
Absent for a lock-projected candidate: `ocx.lock` records the leaf
digest per platform, not the descriptor that pointed at it.

size.description: The candidate manifest's size; absent for a lock-projected candidate.

CandidateOut.description: One platform child of an image index, or one locked platform leaf.

size.description: The layer's size; absent when the descriptor records a negative one.

Layer.description:
A single layer descriptor from the inspected manifest (default mode) or the
platform-selected manifest (`--resolve`).

chain.description: The blobs walked, in order: index when there is one, manifest, config.

Resolution.description:
The OCI resolution chain for the selected platform. Carries only the walk
(`index` → `manifest` → `config`); the platform-selected manifest's layers
are rendered alongside the metadata, not inside the chain.

role.description: What the blob is in the walk: `index`, `manifest` or `config`.

size.description: The blob's size; absent when it is unknown.

ChainOut.description:
One blob in the resolution chain. Same descriptor surface as a layer
(digest, media type, size) plus the OCI `role` so a consumer can tell
the index from the manifest from the config without decoding digests.

deps.description:
Transitive dependencies in transitive-closure order (deps before
dependents). The inspected root is NOT listed here — it is named by the
top-level `identifier` and appears in each surface's attributions.

surface.description: What would land on each axis if the root were installed.

conflicts.description: Conditions on the interface projection that install would refuse.

ClosureOut.description:
The dependency closure emitted with `--closure`. Everything nests under one
object: `deps` (the transitive dependencies in transitive-closure order),
`surface` (the interface + private projections), and interface-projection
`conflicts`.

name.description:
Short display name — the repository's final path segment (e.g.
`deps-mid`). The flat plain tree labels each dep by this.

identifier.description:
Always digest-pinned — a closure node is a resolved artifact, never a
tag. There is no separate `digest` key because this one already ends in
it.

effective_visibility.description: The visibility composed from the root down to this dependency.

binaries.description:
Tri-state, mirrors `Bundle.binaries`: key absent = undeclared,
`Some(empty)` = publisher asserts zero interface executables.

integrations.description:
The dep's own declared integration namespace keys, lexicographically
ordered. Keys only — a closure node is not installed, so
`${installPath}` has no value and an interpolated payload would be a
half-truth. Always present, `[]` when the dep declares none: absent and
empty are the same state here (unlike `binaries`' tri-state).

dependencies.description:
The dep's own declared dependency edges (as authored) — lets a consumer
rebuild the DAG from the flat list.

ClosureDepOut.description: One transitive dependency in the `--closure` object, in transitive-closure order.

name.description: The dependency's name as the edge declares it.

ClosureEdgeOut.description: A declared dependency edge (as authored) of one closure dependency.

interface.description: Consumer-facing: what reaches someone installing the root.

private.description:
Internal: what is visible on the package's own private axis. Public
entries appear in both surfaces (public crosses both axes).

SurfacesOut.description:
The two symmetric surface projections of a closure — "what binaries /
entrypoints / env keys would land, and on which axis, if this were
installed", without installing.

binaries.description: Admitted `binaries` claims on this axis, attributed to their packages.

entrypoints.description: Admitted `entrypoints` claims on this axis, attributed to their packages.

env.description:
Env keys each admitted node exposes on this axis, attributed to the
declaring package. Values are omitted — they are `${installPath}`-
templated and only concrete after install.

integrations.description:
Integration namespace keys each admitted node declares, attributed to
the declaring package. Payload-free — a closure node is not installed,
so `${installPath}` has no value and the payload would be a half-truth,
the same reason `env` omits values.

binaries_complete.description:
`false` iff any admitted node has undeclared `binaries`
("couldn't determine \u{2260} determined zero"). Entrypoints have no
such flag — the entrypoint map keys are always authoritative.

SurfaceOut.description:
One projected surface — binaries/entrypoints/env/integrations admitted on
a single axis.

kind.description: How the value combines with the variable's existing value.

separator.description:
The declared separator for a `list`-kind entry; `None` for every other
kind. Skipped in JSON when `None`.

EnvVarAttribution.description:
One env key exposed on the interface surface, attributed to the package that
declares it. No value: values are `${installPath}`-templated and only concrete after install.

NamespaceAttribution.description:
One integration namespace a closure node declares, attributed to the
declaring package.

No `value`: the closure envelope is payload-free — a closure node is not
installed, so `${installPath}` has no value.

entrypoints.description: Entrypoint names claimed by more than one package.

repositories.description: Repositories resolved to more than one digest.

ConflictsOut.description:
Install/compose-gate conditions detected over the interface projection.
Both arrays always present; empty means the surface is
realizable. Inspect stays a view, not a gate — exit 0 either way.

EntrypointConflictOut.description:
Two or more interface-admitted closure nodes declare the same entrypoint
name.

RepositoryConflictOut.description:
One repository resolved to two or more distinct digests on the interface
projection.

package.description: The package as named, without tag or digest.

repository.description: The repository the tags live in: the index's pointer, else `package`.

dry_run.description: Whether `--dry-run` was in force, so nothing was deleted.

index.description: The index the safeguard judged; absent for a namespace with no configured index.

tags.description: One row per selected tag, in processing order.

PruneOutcome.description: What a run did, in processing order; printed whether or not the run failed.

OciIdentifier.description: OCI registry location in the format 'registry/repository[:tag][@digest]'.

oneOf.description: Exactly these tags, deduplicated, in input order.

prerelease.description: A pre-release without a build, e.g. `0.5.0-canary`.

keep_builds.description:
Keep the newest this many builds and the rolling tag; at least 1.
Absent when every build is selected.

oneOf.description: Every build of one pre-release, plus its rolling tag.

url.description: Where the served root was read from.

root_sha256.description: sha256 of the root bytes as served.

PruneIndexReport.description: The index a run read, as reported.

digest.description: The root row's content, else the digest the registry served; absent when neither is known.

reason.description: Why the tag was kept or refused; absent for every other action.

PruneAction.description: The final state of one selected tag.

x-ocx-enum.description: This run deleted it.
Already gone from the registry.
A dry run would delete it.
Selected, then kept by `--keep-builds`.
The safeguard refused it.
Never reached: an earlier refusal or error stopped the run.

PruneReason.description: Why a tag was kept or refused.

x-ocx-enum.description: One of the newest `--keep-builds` builds.
The pre-release's own tag, kept under `--keep-builds`.
The index lists it without the ephemeral marker.
The registry has it but the index does not list it.

platform.description: The `--platform` the bundle was built for.

identifier.description: The `--identifier` the bundle was built to be pushed as.

PackageReceipt.description:
Report emitted by `ocx package receipt`: what `ocx package create` recorded
beside a bundle.

Plain format: one `label: value` row per recorded field.

JSON format: each key absent when the build did not record it — the same
contract as the file, where absence means "not given", never `null`.

companions.description: Number of companion packages pinned by the snapshot.

descriptors.description: Number of descriptor blobs pinned by the snapshot.

path.description: Absolute path of the written `patches.snapshot.json` file.

PatchFreezeReport.description:
Report emitted by `ocx [--global] patch freeze`.

Plain format: two-column table (`Kind | Count`) summarising how many
companions and descriptors were frozen, followed by the snapshot path.

JSON format: `{ "companions": N, "descriptors": N, "path": "..." }`.

reference.description:
Canonical reference the descriptor was published to
(`registry/repository:__ocx.patch`).

manifest_digest.description: Manifest digest of the pushed `__ocx.patch` artifact.

rules.description: Number of rules in the published descriptor.

PatchPublishReport.description:
Report emitted by `ocx [--global] patch publish`.

Plain format: a single-row table (`Reference | Digest | Rules`) showing the
published patch repo reference, the manifest digest, and the descriptor rule
count.

bases_checked.description: Number of installed bases (plus global root) that were checked.

descriptors_updated.description: Number of descriptor blobs where the upstream digest advanced.

companions_installed.description: Number of companion packages installed or re-installed.

PatchSyncReport.description:
Report emitted by `ocx [--global] patch sync`.

Plain format: a single-row summary table (`Checked | Updated | Companions`)
showing how many bases were checked, descriptors updated, and companions
installed.

JSON format: `{ "bases_checked": N, "descriptors_updated": N, "companions_installed": N }`.

base.description: The base identifier the descriptor was composed onto.

companions.description: Companion identifiers that matched the base under the descriptor's rules.

items.description: Composed env entries: the base's interface surface (private under `--self`), then the companion overlay.

PatchTestReport.description:
Report emitted by `ocx patch test` (env-inspection mode, no script/command).

Shows which companions the descriptor matched for the base identifier and
the composed environment that results from overlaying them.

Plain format: a hint line naming the matched companions, followed by a table
of composed env entries (`Key | Type | Value`, plus a `Source` column naming
the rule glob + companion when any overlay entry is present).

kind.description: How the value folds into the environment.

separator.description: The separator a `list` entry folds with; omitted for every other `kind`.

source.description: Provenance for a companion overlay entry; `None` for base-native entries.

PatchTestEntry.description:
A single composed environment variable entry shown by `ocx patch test`.

The `source` object has the same shape `--show-patches` reports.

items.description: One entry per contributed variable; empty when no companion applies or none adds a var here.

PatchWhyReport.description:
`ocx patch why <base>`: each env var a companion contributes to `base`, with the matching rule
and companion. Empty is never an error: either no companion applies, or those that apply add
nothing to this surface.

rule.description: The descriptor rule `match` glob that admitted the companion.

companion.description: The companion that produced the var.

PatchWhyEntry.description:
A single env var an infrastructure-patch companion contributes to a base.

`variable` is the env var name, `rule` is the descriptor rule `match` glob
that admitted the companion for the base, and `companion` is the identifier
of the companion that produced the var.

paths.description: Each located package, keyed by the identifier as given, in request order.

kind.description: Whether `path` is a package root or a shim tree.

LocatedPath.description:
One located package: the directory `ocx package which` reports for it, and
which kind of directory that is.

A tool composed lazily has no package directory until its first invocation
materializes one, so the answer to "where is this on disk" is its generated
shim tree. `kind` tells the two apart.

PathKind.description:
What kind of directory a reported `path` names.

A tool composed lazily has no package directory until its first invocation
materializes one — what exists on disk is its generated shim tree. `ocx pull`
and `ocx package which` both report this same two-value vocabulary.

x-ocx-enum.description: The package root: the parent of `content/` and `entrypoints/`.

The generated shim directory of a deferred tool. Its `bin/` holds one
launcher per declared name; the package directory does not exist yet.

paths.description: Each package root, keyed by the identifier as given, in request order.

Paths.description: Resolved package roots for `ocx package pull`.

items.description: One entry per locked tool, in lock-file order.

PullDryRun.description: Preview of what `ocx pull` would do without writing to the store.

status.description: Whether the tool is cached or would be fetched.

path.description: The package root; absent when nothing is materialised yet.

DryRunEntry.description:
A single dry-run preview row.

`path` is the package root directory (parent of `content/` and
`entrypoints/`) for `cached` rows and absent for `would_fetch` rows, where
nothing has been materialised yet.

PullStatus.description:
Whether a locked tool is already in the object store or would be
fetched on a real `ocx pull`.

x-ocx-enum.description: Already in the object store.
A real `ocx pull` would download it.

identifier.description:
The pushed package, carrying the tag actually written — the
`--build-timestamp` suffix included — not the tag the caller passed.

status.description: Outcome of the push.

manifest_digest.description: Digest of the pushed multi-platform image index.

cascade_tags_written.description:
Rolling cascade tags written in addition to the primary version tag
(e.g. `3.28`, `3`, `latest`). Empty for a non-cascade push.

keep_tags_written.description:
Digest-named `__ocx.keep.<algorithm>-<hex>` tags this push wrote, in
push order, one
per distinct platform manifest — platforms whose manifest is identical
share a single tag, so this does not zip against the pushed platform
list. Empty under `--no-keep-tag`. Reports what reached the
registry, not what was requested.

layers.description:
Counts of layer-push outcomes (mounted/uploaded/verified), summed over
every platform this push fanned out to. Layer blobs only — the config
blob and manifest are not layers.

platform_digests.description:
Platform manifest digests this push produced, keyed by the canonical
platform string (`os/arch[/variant][+feature,…]`), sorted.

The signing input for a later `push --sign`, fully populated even under
`--no-keep-tag`. Two platforms sharing one manifest appear as two keys
with one value. Distinct from `manifest_digest`, the tag's image index,
which every platform merge rewrites, so a signature cannot cover it.
JSON only.

annotations_written.description:
Every OCI annotation this push wrote onto the index of each tag it
touched — the `--ci-annotations` set with the explicit `--annotation`
pairs laid over it. Empty (and omitted) for a push that annotates
nothing.

What landed, not what was asked for: a `--ci-annotations` key whose
variable was unset is absent here, which is how a pipeline finds out
that its runner did not export what it assumed. JSON only.

aliases_written.description:
The un-prefixed track tags `--default` aliased onto this push, bare
version first (`1.2.3`, then `1.2`, `1`, `latest` under `--cascade`).
Empty (and omitted) without the flag, and for a push whose tag carries
no variant. JSON only. Each alias is an index write onto manifests this
push already uploaded, never a second upload.

signatures.description:
One row per platform manifest `--sign` signed inline, in push order.

Empty (and omitted) without `--sign`. JSON only; a signing failure also
reaches a plain caller on stderr. The image index is never listed:
platform manifest digests are final once pushed, but the index digest is
rewritten on every platform merge, so `ocx package sign --tags-file`
signs it later.

attestation.description:
Absent unless `--sbom` was passed.

Reported separately from `status`, which reports the push alone: a push
that lands and an attestation that then fails is a real state — the
manifest is immutable and OCI offers no un-push.

PushReport.description:
Result of a successful `ocx package push`.

`ocx-mirror pipeline push` keys its go/no-go off `status` and records
`cascade_tags_written`. `platform_digests`, `annotations_written`,
`aliases_written`, `signatures` and `attestation` are omitted when empty,
so an unsigned push that annotates nothing emits the first six keys alone.

x-ocx-enum.description: The push landed; the registry merge is idempotent, so a repeat push lands too.

mounted.description:
Layers a cross-repository blob mount placed in the target repository
without any upload.

uploaded.description:
Layers uploaded rather than mounted or verified.

A layer the registry already held may still count here, so this does
not strictly mean "bytes crossed the wire".

verified.description: Layers referenced by digest and confirmed already present in the registry.

LayerCounts.description:
Aggregate counts of layer-push outcomes for a single package push.

Only layer blobs are counted — the config blob and the manifest itself
are not layers and are excluded. The counts distinguish mount vs. explicit
upload vs. verify-by-digest, not whether bytes actually crossed the wire:
an `uploaded` layer may still have been skipped as already present.

platform.description:
The platform whose manifest was signed; its canonical spelling keys
`platform_digests`.

status.description: What the inline signing did to this platform.

report.description:
That platform's own sign report, verbatim. Present for every platform
whose run produced one, `failed` rows included: a
`--signature-format both` platform where one leg landed and one did not
is a failure that still carries the leg that landed.

kind.description:
The error's slug, else its category: the `error.detail`, else the
`error.kind`, its error document would carry. Present exactly when
`status` is `failed`.

message.description:
Human-readable cause, sanitized for the terminal (CWE-150). Present
exactly when `status` is `failed`.

SignedPlatformReport.description:
One platform manifest's inline-signing row.

Shaped like an `ocx package sign` sweep row with `tag` replaced by
`platform`: `status` shares its vocabulary and `report` is a sign report
verbatim, so code parsing an `ocx package sign` document parses this one
level down. `status` is never `skipped` here: a platform the merged index
did not carry is omitted from `platform_digests` and never becomes a row.

SweptStatus.description: What the sweep did to one tag; one vocabulary for both verbs.

x-ocx-enum.description: The tag's index was acted on; `report` carries the outcome.

The tag resolved to a bare manifest, so the sweep left it alone.

Not a failure, and it does not make the run exit non-zero: `push`
already signed each platform manifest inline, and a tag list mixing
single-platform and multi-platform packages is the normal case for a
repository publishing both.

The tag names the index another tag in this same sweep already acted on,
so one referrer covers both and nothing was written for this tag.

Not a failure, and it does not make the run exit non-zero: the tag *is*
signed (or attested), by the referrer the covering tag's row reports.
`message` names that tag.

This tag failed. The sweep carried on to the rest and the run exits
non-zero at the end.

identifier.description: The package that was signed, resolved against the default registry.

subject_digest.description: Digest of the subject manifest that the bundle signs.

legs.description:
One entry per wire shape that was written or attempted, in write order.

`--signature-format both` emits two **independent** signatures, so the
run is best-effort per leg rather than atomic: a leg that failed is
reported alongside one that succeeded, and the exit code comes from the
failure.

platform.description:
The `--platform` the run narrowed into; absent when none was given and
the run signed whatever the identifier resolved to.

signer.description: Signing mechanism used: `"keyless-fulcio"`, or the key backend's own slug under a key.

certificate_identity.description:
Certificate SAN (identity) embedded in the Fulcio cert. Absent under a
key, and when no leg was written.

certificate_oidc_issuer.description:
Certificate OIDC issuer URL embedded in the Fulcio cert. Absent under a
key, and when no leg was written.

key_backend.description:
Which key model produced this signature: `keyless`, `file`, or a
key-backend scheme.

public_key_hint.description: The signing key's cosign hint, in key mode only.

transparency_log_index.description:
The Rekor log index of the transparency record this run created.

Absent when no record was created: legal under a key, where
`--rekor-upload` is opt-in.

SignatureReport.description:
Summary of a signing operation, keyless or under a key.

Digests are always full in JSON. A leg's two digests are not
interchangeable: `payload_digest` is the SHA-256 of the signed blob (what
the transparency record covers), `manifest_digest` that of the manifest it
hangs from. `signer` is `"keyless-fulcio"`, or the key backend's own slug
under a key. A partial run (one leg failed) still prints this report and
exits non-zero.

payload_digest.description:
Digest of the signed payload blob — the Sigstore bundle under `bundle`,
the simplesigning claim under `simplesigning`. Absent when the leg failed.

manifest_digest.description:
Digest of the manifest the payload hangs from — the OCI referrer under
`bundle`, the `sha256-<hex>.sig` sidecar under `simplesigning`.

error.description: Why the leg failed, when it did. `None` means it was written.

SignatureLegReport.description: One wire shape's outcome, as reported.

SignatureFormat.description:
Which cosign wire shape a signature is written in, and which shape a verify
pins.

Format and key model are **orthogonal**: either format can be produced
keyless or with a key pair, so this value never says anything about how the
signing material was obtained.

x-ocx-enum.description:
An OCI 1.1 referrer carrying a Sigstore bundle v0.3. The default, and
the only shape `cosign sign` v3 produces against a registry that
implements the Referrers API.

The cosign `sha256-<hex>.sig` sidecar tag, whose layers carry
simplesigning payloads.

Write both shapes.

**Write-side only**: a verify pins exactly one shape, and the read-side
resolver refuses this value.

status.description: Whether the attestation was published.

referrer_digest.description:
Digest of the published OCI referrer manifest. Absent on failure, and
under `--signature-format simplesigning`, which publishes the
`sha256-<hex>.att` sidecar alone and no referrer.

sidecar_digest.description:
Digest of the `sha256-<hex>.att` sidecar manifest, when
`--signature-format` asked for one. Spelled as in the
`ocx package attest` report, so one vocabulary names both addresses.

predicate_type.description:
The resolved `predicateType` URI written into the Statement. Present
exactly when `status` is `succeeded`.

signed.description:
Whether the referrer carries a signature. `false` means the SBOM was
attached raw because the run had no signing identity available — the
push still succeeded, and nothing vouches for the document. Present
exactly when `status` is `succeeded`.

kind.description:
The error document's `error.detail` slug, falling back to its
`error.kind` category. Present exactly when `status` is `failed`.

message.description:
Human-readable cause, sanitized for the terminal (CWE-150). Present
exactly when `status` is `failed`.

AttestationOutcome.description:
What `--sbom` did after the push landed.

A failure carries the error slug the JSON error document would have used,
not a bespoke string, so a script branches on the same vocabulary
either way.

x-ocx-enum.description: The attestation was published on the pushed manifest.
The push landed and was NOT rolled back; the attestation did not.

items.description: One entry per package, in request order.

Removed.description: Results of an uninstall or deselect; `path` gets no plain column since it names something now gone.

status.description: What happened to it.

path.description: What was removed; absent when nothing was.

RemovedEntry.description:
A single uninstall or deselect result entry.

The `path` field holds the symlink that was removed (for `removed`) or the
object directory that was purged (for `purged`), and is absent when the
resource was already absent.

RemovedStatus.description: Whether the resource was actually removed, purged, or was already absent.

x-ocx-enum.description: The symlink was removed.
The package's object directory was deleted.
Nothing was there to remove.

summary.description:
One-glance counts, so a consumer branches on a field instead of
measuring an array.

attestations.description: One entry per listed attestation, in listing order.

refused.description:
Every candidate examined and refused, in listing order. Never
truncated in JSON.

SbomListingReport.description: Every verified attestation a package carries, plus what was refused.

status.description: Whether any candidate was refused.

verification.description: Which trust contract produced this listing: `verified` or `unverified`.

total.description: `verified + unverified + refused` — every candidate the scan examined.

unverified.description:
Documents no signature was checked for. Counted apart from
`verified` so a script branches on the trust class instead of
filtering the array — an unverified document is a real answer to "what
SBOMs does this carry" and not a real answer to "who vouches for them".

ListingSummary.description: The counts and the status a script branches on.

ListingStatus.description:
Whether every examined candidate was listed.

A refusal beside a listing is a partial failure the caller is told about and
the run still exits 0, even when every document refused under `--summary`.
Only a zero-match scan exits non-zero (79), and it prints no listing.

x-ocx-enum.description: Nothing was refused.
At least one candidate was refused; see `refused`.

ListingVerification.description:
Which trust contract the whole listing was produced under.

Under `verified` an unverified row cannot occur (an unsigned attachment is
