refused, not listed), so every entry carries a checked signature. Under
`unverified` nothing was checked and every entry is unverified, even one a
publisher signed: this run has no evidence to tell them apart.

x-ocx-enum.description: Signatures were checked against the resolved policies.
Nothing was checked; every row is unverified.

verified.description:
Whether a signature was verified over this document.

`false` means the SBOM was attached raw, with no identity behind it:
the registry served bytes and said what they are. The three fields
below are then absent rather than empty.

shadowed.description:
`true` when a platform-level SBOM of the **same predicateType**
supersedes this index-level one. A shadowed entry stays listed under
`--format json`; only the human default collapses to the preferred one.

Emitted unconditionally: `false` is a *true* statement — nothing
supersedes this document — so a consumer can branch on the key without
first testing for its presence.

subject_digest.description:
The target digest. Proven bound by the signed Statement when
`verified`; claimed by the referrer otherwise.

referrer_digest.description:
What carried the document — **not always a manifest**.

Almost always the OCI referrer manifest's digest; the **layer** blob's
digest in exactly one case, a verified attestation read off a cosign
`sha256-<hex>.att` sidecar tag (one layer is one document), where
`GET /v2/<name>/manifests/<digest>` 404s. This row carries no
discriminator: to address the digest, read the same subject through
`ocx package verify --attestation --format json`, whose `signatures[]`
rows carry `signature_format`.

certificate_identity.description: Certificate SAN (identity) embedded in the Fulcio cert.

certificate_oidc_issuer.description: Certificate OIDC issuer embedded in the Fulcio cert.

signed_at.description: Rekor integrated time. Absent when no transparency record exists or its time is unrepresentable.

SbomSummaryOut.description: What `--summary` reports for one CycloneDX document.

referrer_digest.description:
The referrer's digest as the registry listed it. Absent when no
well-formed digest names the candidate: a budget-stop row, or a
registry listing a malformed digest.

reason.description:
Why this candidate was refused, as prose for a human. Registry-sourced
either way: several kinds quote a field read off the wire.

reason_kind.description:
The same refusal as a frozen slug.

Branch on this, never on `reason`: the prose is English and free to be
reworded, and substring-matching it is how a consumer silently stops
matching.

RefusedEntry.description: One candidate that was examined and refused.

status.description: Overall status (the structured mirror of the exit code).

assertion.description: The terminating assertion record; absent unless the run failed on one.

run.description: Surfaced `RunResult` fields; absent unless a terminal `ocx.run` is reported.

ScriptRunReport.description:
The `--script` result envelope.

Plain format: one human status line on stdout.

ScriptStatus.description:
Overall outcome of a scripted test run. Mirrors
`ocx_script::ScriptOutcomeKind` at the OCX-facing level.

x-ocx-enum.description: Script ran to completion; all assertions passed.
An assertion failed, `expect.fail`/`fail()`, or a host-fn failure.
The script could not be used as given (unreadable script file).
Syntax / arity / type error in the script source.
A sandboxed filesystem operation failed for I/O reasons.
The wall-clock budget elapsed before the script finished.

message.description: Failure detail. For `expect.ok`, auto-embeds the child stderr.

location.description:
Where in the script the failure happened. Additive-optional: absent for
an outcome the engine could not locate (a timeout, a pre-engine host
fault), never emitted as `null`.

AssertionRecord.description:
The terminating assertion record (when the run failed on an assertion).

`message` prose is non-stable; its presence and field shape are contractual.

file.description: The label the script source was parsed under.

SourceLocation.description:
Source position of a script failure.

JSON format: `{"file": "tests/smoke.star", "line": 12, "column": 5}`. Line
and column are 1-indexed. `file` is the label the source was parsed under —
the verbatim `--script` path, or `<stdin>` for the `--script -` form, which
names no file a reporter can open.

exit_code.description: Child exit code (or `128 + signal` when signal-killed).

truncated.description: `true` iff stdout or stderr hit the capture cap.

RunSummary.description: Surfaced `RunResult` fields for the script's terminal/top-level `ocx.run`.

status.description: The run's overall outcome; `skipped` when a managed block was left dirty.

bootstrap.description: Whether this run installed ocx into its own content store.

shims.description: The env shim files this run wrote.

profiles.description: One entry per shell profile this run considered.

session_path_stores.description:
One entry per session-PATH store this host owns, the skipped ones included; empty only
where the platform has no session-PATH facility.

dirty_profiles.description:
Profiles skipped because the user edited the managed block; present iff
status = `skipped`. Carried separately for a script to `case` on without
scanning the `profiles` list.

conflicting_ocx.description: An `ocx` on `PATH` ahead of the directory the shim prepends, if found.

reload_hint.description:
Whether this run changed a PATH surface that the user must act on: a shim or
managed profile block (re-source the shell), or a session-PATH store (log out
and back in, so programs started outside a shell see it too).

extra_ca_certs.description:
Result of persisting `OCX_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` into `config.toml`.

Always present; only `certificates` is omitted, on `not_configured`. The
plain table suppresses its row the same way `managed_config`'s does, when
`not_configured`.

SelfSetupData.description:
Report of `ocx self setup`.

Plain format: a key/value table (`Status`, `Bootstrap`, written shims,
per-profile outcomes, and any advisory), with empty rows suppressed.

SelfSetupStatus.description: The overall outcome of an `ocx self setup` run; `skipped` exits 81, every other status 0.

x-ocx-enum.description: Shims and/or profiles were written or upgraded.
Nothing changed — every shim and profile was already current.
At least one profile carried user edits and was left untouched.
A legacy footprint was migrated to the v1 fence.

status.description: What the bootstrap did.

version.description: The version pulled, or that a dry run would pull.

digest.description: Resolved content digest; present when a pinned version produced one.

BootstrapEntry.description: Whether this run installed ocx into its own content store.

x-ocx-enum.description: The requested ocx was already installed.
The requested ocx was pulled.
Dry run: the requested ocx would be pulled.

outcome.description: What this run did to the profile's managed block.

ProfileEntry.description: One shell profile and what this run did to its managed block.

ProfileOutcomeKind.description: What a run did to one profile's managed block.

x-ocx-enum.description: The managed block was written or upgraded.
The managed block was already current.
A legacy footprint was migrated to the current fence.
The managed block carried user edits and was left untouched.

location.description: Where the store lives: a file, or a registry location on Windows.

outcome.description: What this run did to the store.

SessionPathEntry.description: One session-PATH store and what this run did to it.

SessionPathOutcomeKind.description: What a run did to one session-PATH store.

x-ocx-enum.description: The ocx directories were written to the store.
The store already held the ocx directories.
The ocx directories were removed from the store.
Skipped: PATH modification is opted out.
Skipped: this host has no such store.
Writing the store failed; the run warned and carried on.

status.description: What the run did with the extra CA roots.

certificates.description: How many certificates the resolved value holds; absent on `not_configured` and `system_locked`.

ExtraCaCertsStatusKind.description: What a run did with the extra CA roots.

x-ocx-enum.description: `OCX_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` is not set.
`config.toml` already holds the same roots.
The roots were written to `config.toml`.
Dry run: the roots would be written to `config.toml`.
The system tier locks the setting, so nothing was validated or written.

status.description: What the update did.

from.description:
Previously installed version; present on `installed` and `pulled` when
the old binary's version query succeeded. Absent when that query was not
available (binary absent, non-zero exit, malformed JSON output).

to.description: Newly downloaded version; present iff status is `installed` or `pulled`.

skipped_reason.description: Why the update was skipped; present iff status = `skipped`.

handoff.description:
How the hand-off to the new binary's own `ocx self setup` ended, when it
did not end cleanly. Present on `installed` (the swap landed, some setup
surface may not have been written) and on `pulled` (nothing was
activated); absent whenever the child completed.

SelfUpdateStatus.description: Outcome of an update check or a self-update.

x-ocx-enum.description: The installed version is the latest.
The check did not run; `skipped_reason` says why.
A newer version is available (`--check`).
A newer version was pulled and activated.

The release was downloaded but nothing was activated — `current` still
names the previously installed binary.

oneOf.description: The installed version could not be queried, so the check cannot compare versions.
Offline mode blocked the registry probe.
The 24-hour throttle window has not elapsed since the last probe.
The registry probe failed.
The package was not found in the registry.
The installed version string is not a version.
The registry's latest tag is not a version.
The registry lists no `major.minor.patch` release tag.

SkippedReason.description: Why an update check was skipped.

oneOf.description: The new binary could not be started.
The new binary's setup exited non-zero; `81` means it left a user-edited profile alone.
The new binary's setup was killed by a signal (Unix only).

HandoffFailure.description: How the hand-off to the new binary's own `ocx self setup` ended, when it did not end cleanly.

status.description: What the check found.

identifier.description: Identifier of the available update; present iff status = `update_available`.

skipped_reason.description: Why the check was skipped; present iff status = `skipped`.

ocx_home.description:
`$OCX_HOME`.

A missing home is an ordinary state on a fresh install and exits 0; only
a home that cannot be *read* exits 74.

shell_integration_installed.description:
Whether `ocx self setup` has ever wired this machine's shell.

Probed as the witness shim under `ocx_home`.

toolchain_home.description:
The **resolved toolchain home**, a machine-readable contract field.

The supported way for an IDE, a devcontainer feature or a CI step to find
a project's tree when `config.toml` relocates it with `toolchain_dir`:
`<project>/.ocx/toolchain` or `<toolchain_dir>/<project-key>/toolchain`
for the project in effect, and `$OCX_HOME/toolchain` when no project
resolves. **Always present, never `null`**: an invalid `toolchain_dir`
fails config load with exit 78 instead.

toolchain_bin.description:
The **PATH-facing trampoline directory** for the same tier, which a consumer outside ocx puts on `PATH`.

`toolchain_home` answers *where the tree is*; this answers *what to
export*, and the two are not one join apart, so never build this from
`toolchain_home`. Always present. It
names a directory that need not exist yet: a home that has never been
pulled reports the path it *would* hold.

activate.description:
The **effective** `activate` mode, past the whole ladder.

The flag tier (absent here), then `ocx.toml`, then
`OCX_TOOLCHAIN_ACTIVATE`, then the floor. The resolved answer, never a tier.

pinned.description:
The **effective** `pinned` value, resolved through the same ladder.

`true` means a composing emitter yields digest paths and consults no
`links/<group>/<entry>` link; `false` means it follows the rendered links, so
an `ocx update` takes effect with no re-render.

lock_refusal.description:
Why the project's `ocx.lock` refuses composition, when it does, as text.

Set when consent activates over a lock composition refuses, such as a
`paths` grant over an unreadable or stale lock. Every prompt then exits 65
and the scope never reaches the ledger.

carrier_present.description:
Whether the `__OCX_ENV_STATE` carrier is set at all.

This is what separates two inert states: an absent
carrier is the first prompt of a shell (nothing applied, nothing to
repair); a carrier that is present and undecodable is a corrupt one (a
scope was applied and its record is gone).

carrier_bytes.description: The carrier's encoded length in bytes, measured against the carrier cap.

ledger.description:
The decoded ledger, **rendered as fields, never as base64**.

Schema `v` and the payload; absent when the carrier is absent or fails to
decode. Carries what is applied per scope (`global` and `project`

keep_tags_written.description:
Digest-named `__ocx.keep.<algorithm>-<hex>` tags this push wrote, in

list. Empty under `--no-keep-tag`. Reports what reached the

platform_digests.description:
Platform manifest digests this push produced, keyed by the canonical
platform string (`os/arch[/variant][+feature,…]`), sorted.

The signing input for a later `push --sign`, fully populated even under
`--no-keep-tag`. Two platforms sharing one manifest appear as two keys
with one value. Distinct from `manifest_digest`, the tag's image index,
which every platform merge rewrites, so a signature cannot cover it.
JSON only.

annotations_written.description:
Every OCI annotation this push wrote onto the index of each tag it
touched — the `--ci-annotations` set with the explicit `--annotation`
pairs laid over it. Empty (and omitted) for a push that annotates
nothing.

What landed, not what was asked for: a `--ci-annotations` key whose
variable was unset is absent here, which is how a pipeline finds out
that its runner did not export what it assumed. JSON only.

aliases_written.description:
The un-prefixed track tags `--default` aliased onto this push, bare
version first (`1.2.3`, then `1.2`, `1`, `latest` under `--cascade`).
Empty (and omitted) without the flag, and for a push whose tag carries
no variant. JSON only. Each alias is an index write onto manifests this
push already uploaded, never a second upload.

signatures.description:
One row per platform manifest `--sign` signed inline, in push order.

Empty (and omitted) without `--sign`. JSON only; a signing failure also
reaches a plain caller on stderr. The image index is never listed:
platform manifest digests are final once pushed, but the index digest is
rewritten on every platform merge, so `ocx package sign --tags-file`
signs it later.

attestation.description:
Absent unless `--sbom` was passed.

Reported separately from `status`, which reports the push alone: a push
that lands and an attestation that then fails is a real state — the
manifest is immutable and OCI offers no un-push.

PushReportRoot.description:
Result of a successful `ocx package push`.

`ocx-mirror pipeline push` keys its go/no-go off `status` and records
`cascade_tags_written`. `platform_digests`, `annotations_written`,
`aliases_written`, `signatures` and `attestation` are omitted when empty,
so an unsigned push that annotates nothing emits the first six keys alone.

toolchain_home.description:
The **resolved toolchain home**, a machine-readable contract field.

The supported way for an IDE, a devcontainer feature or a CI step to find
a project's tree when `config.toml` relocates it with `toolchain_dir`:
`<project>/.ocx/toolchain` or `<toolchain_dir>/<project-key>/toolchain`
for the project in effect, and `$OCX_HOME/toolchain` when no project
resolves. **Always present, never `null`**: an invalid `toolchain_dir`
fails config load with exit 78 instead.

toolchain_bin.description:
The **PATH-facing trampoline directory** for the same tier, which a consumer outside ocx puts on `PATH`.

`toolchain_home` answers *where the tree is*; this answers *what to
export*, and the two are not one join apart, so never build this from
`toolchain_home`. Always present. It
names a directory that need not exist yet: a home that has never been
pulled reports the path it *would* hold.

activate.description:
The **effective** `activate` mode, past the whole ladder.

The flag tier (absent here), then `ocx.toml`, then
`OCX_TOOLCHAIN_ACTIVATE`, then the floor. The resolved answer, never a tier.

pinned.description:
The **effective** `pinned` value, resolved through the same ladder.

`true` means a composing emitter yields digest paths and consults no
`links/<group>/<entry>` link; `false` means it follows the rendered links, so
an `ocx update` takes effect with no re-render.

lock_refusal.description:
Why the project's `ocx.lock` refuses composition, when it does, as text.

Set when consent activates over a lock composition refuses, such as a
`paths` grant over an unreadable or stale lock. Every prompt then exits 65
and the scope never reaches the ledger.

carrier_present.description:
Whether the `__OCX_ENV_STATE` carrier is set at all.

This is what separates two inert states: an absent
carrier is the first prompt of a shell (nothing applied, nothing to
repair); a carrier that is present and undecodable is a corrupt one (a
scope was applied and its record is gone).

carrier_bytes.description: The carrier's encoded length in bytes, measured against the carrier cap.

ledger.description:
The decoded ledger, **rendered as fields, never as base64**.

Schema `v` and the payload; absent when the carrier is absent or fails to
decode. Carries what is applied per scope (`global` and `project`
separately), the recorded prior of each constant the project scope owns
(the one datum nothing can reconstruct) and, through `over_cap`, the
abandoned-scope marker.

fingerprint_current.description:
Whether the ledger's recorded `fp` still matches the watch set on disk now.

Absent when there is no recorded fingerprint to compare against, **and**
when no fold is available to compare with.

watch_set.description: The watch set, with each member's presence, size and modification time.

project_dir.description: The project the CWD walk resolved, canonicalized; absent when none resolved.

project_key.description: The 16-hex state key of `project_dir`; absent with it.

project_stamped.description:
Whether a usable consent stamp exists for that key; an unusable stamp
counts as absent.

grant.description:
**Which clause activated this project**; absent when it is inert.

A consent stamp outranks the `[shell.consent]` table.

stamp_written_at.description:

The stamp's own recorded instant, not its file time. Absent whenever

priors.description: Prior intactness for each constant the ledger's project scope owns.

identifier.description: The package that was signed, resolved against the default registry.

subject_digest.description: Digest of the subject manifest that the bundle signs.

legs.description:
One entry per wire shape that was written or attempted, in write order.

`--signature-format both` emits two **independent** signatures, so the
run is best-effort per leg rather than atomic: a leg that failed is
reported alongside one that succeeded, and the exit code comes from the
failure.

platform.description:
The `--platform` the run narrowed into; absent when none was given and
the run signed whatever the identifier resolved to.

signer.description: Signing mechanism used: `"keyless-fulcio"`, or the key backend's own slug under a key.

certificate_identity.description:
Certificate SAN (identity) embedded in the Fulcio cert. Absent under a
key, and when no leg was written.

certificate_oidc_issuer.description:
Certificate OIDC issuer URL embedded in the Fulcio cert. Absent under a
key, and when no leg was written.

key_backend.description:
Which key model produced this signature: `keyless`, `file`, or a
key-backend scheme.

public_key_hint.description: The signing key's cosign hint, in key mode only.

transparency_log_index.description:
The Rekor log index of the transparency record this run created.

Absent when no record was created: legal under a key, where
`--rekor-upload` is opt-in.

SignatureReportRoot.description:
Summary of a signing operation, keyless or under a key.

Digests are always full in JSON. A leg's two digests are not
interchangeable: `payload_digest` is the SHA-256 of the signed blob (what
the transparency record covers), `manifest_digest` that of the manifest it
hangs from. `signer` is `"keyless-fulcio"`, or the key backend's own slug
under a key. A partial run (one leg failed) still prints this report and
exits non-zero.
